To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) stimulation of the hypothalamic area in the brain produces a generalized reaction which resembles the acute-phase reaction of inflammation; (b) stimulation of this region in animals produces a reaction which includes the release of a number of hormones, including corticotropin, growth hormone, and ACTH, and (c) this hypothalamic reaction is inhibited or blocked by the administration of morphine or by the surgical interruption of the hypothalamospinal tract.

(1) the nervous system is capable of influencing the inflammatory response in animals and in man, (2) the nervous system may influence the inflammatory response through the autonomic nervous system and through the hypothalamus, and (3) the nervous system can influence the inflammatory response in a manner independent of the autonomic nervous and the hypothalamus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the nervous system on the inflammatory process and with the possible participation of the nervous system in the pathogenesis of disease.
the role of the nervous system as a modulating influence in disease processes, and with the mechanisms by which this influence may be exerted.
the effects of nervous activity on the inflammatory response, with particular attention to the effects of emotional stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nervous system participates in the inflammatory reaction, and in the initiation and maintenance of disease, in a variety of ways.

, in the absence of direct evidence of neural involvement, it is impossible to state with assurance whether the nervous system is involved in the inflammatory reaction, or in the initiation of the disease process.
there are no data which demonstrate that the nervous system is essential for the initiation or maintenance of the inflammatory response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nervous system may influence disease processes through its effects on the immune system and on the vascular system.
the nervous system is involved in the inflammatory reaction, but that its role in the pathogenesis and course of disease is complex and not yet fully understood.

the nervous system may influence pathological reactions through the following mechanisms: (1) through its influence on the autonomic nervous system; (2) through its influence over the secretion of hormones; (3) through its influence upon the immune system.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in addition to its role in initiating disease, the nervous system may also play a part in the course of the disease process, in the response of the body to the presence of disease, and in the response of disease to therapy.
the central nervous system is involved in the initiation of the inflammatory response.
the nervous system can influence inflammatory reactions and the initiation of disease through the mediation of a variety of humoral factors, and also by influencing the activity of the immune system.
